authors, or founders, but we evaluate them as if
only the final answer matters. This position pa-
per argues that outcome-only evaluation is insuffi-
cient, and that task outcome, mechanism fidelity,

rately. Our evidence comes from 28 episodes of
a coding agent attempting to rediscover a known
particle identification observable in a Geant4 sim-
ulation, including an 8-episode probe across two
additional frontier models. In 4/20 primary-model
and 3/8 cross-model episodes, agents reach right-
looking results through incorrect reasoning that
breaks when conditions change, which we call
Correct Answer, Wrong Mechanism(CAWM).

a single agent trajectory. When given a partially
misleading prior, all five agents reject the false

pattern.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Mechanism claims are checked against pooled simulation data, per-episode recomputations, and an external regime-shift script, with contradictions documented in the agents' own tables.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: The headline CAWM coding and verification are established by recomputing observables from the agents' own simulation data and comparing stated mechanisms against ground-truth Geant4 physics across impact-parameter regimes.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The agents are pre-trained models prompted with four fixed prompt variants; no training, tuning, reward, selection, or other adaptation loop operates on the task, and the proposed regime-shift check is applied post-hoc without modifying the agents.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims are carefully calibrated to existence rather than population prevalence [Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0037, Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0048, Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0051]. The empirical evidence solidly demonstrates that epistemic honesty under prior falsification dissociates from mechanism fidelity during claim defense [Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0023, Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0032, Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0033].
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation includes detailed quantitative audits of 20 primary episodes (Claude Opus 4.6) and an 8-episode cross-model probe (Gemini 2.5 Flash and Pro), analyzing observable stability across parameter regimes [Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0021, Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0024, Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0035]. The proposed out-of-regime check and companion recomputation successfully catch all seven CAWM cases, establishing consistent diagnostic utility on the studied sample [Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0045].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Agent claims and mechanism explanations are audited directly against ground-truth simulation event data, including pooled runs across impact parameters and an external regime-shift script.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Post-hoc coding and verification of physical explanations against underlying Geant4 simulation data and cross-regime recomputation.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Pre-trained agent models prompting and baseline guidance; agents operate autonomously without internal fine-tuning or optimization loops on the task.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently discuss key limitations, including reliance on a single particle-physics simulation domain, small sample sizes (N=5 per prompt; N=1 for cross-model probes), single-author post-hoc coding, and focus on single-agent loops rather than multi-agent systems [Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0051, Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0052, Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0053].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is well-designed and controlled, executing 28 automated agent trajectories across four prompt conditions spanning an information gradient (open-ended discovery, structured scaffolding, positive control, and biased prior) using a Geant4 Cherenkov detector simulation [Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0002, Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0013, Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0021]. The coding definitions for CAWM, detectable failures, and outcome correctness are explicitly formalized and grounded in direct data recomputations [Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0014, Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0018, Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0019].
primary.quality_rationale: The paper provides an insightful, rigorous, and clearly scoped contribution to the evaluation of AI agents in science, exposing how outcome-level metrics fail to capture flawed mechanistic justifications and demonstrating an effective cross-regime audit check.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript presents a controlled empirical case study and position demonstrating 'Correct Answer, Wrong Mechanism' (CAWM) in LLM scientific agents, showing that agents can produce apparently correct discriminants while justifying them with physics contradicted by their own data or overgeneralized across regimes [Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0002, Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0007, Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0011]. It also proposes and validates a lightweight regime-shift verification protocol to detect such failures [Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0039, Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0045].

scholarly_quality.rationale: The paper provides an insightful, rigorous, and clearly scoped contribution to the evaluation of AI agents in science, exposing how outcome-level metrics fail to capture flawed mechanistic justifications and demonstrating an effective cross-regime audit check.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors transparently discuss key limitations, including reliance on a single particle-physics simulation domain, small sample sizes (N=5 per prompt; N=1 for cross-model probes), single-author post-hoc coding, and focus on single-agent loops rather than multi-agent systems [Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0051, Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0052, Eeebd3aad7c17b63e-B0053].
